svg.title: One core, many homes
svg.desc: Three homes (Kubernetes, standalone, Slurm) differ only in how the grant arrives, how readiness is published, which cgroup the agent owns, what endpoint callers dial, what the fabric channel is and what scope the home asserts; the core (agent, ledger, fences, budget, host runtime and backends) is identical beneath each and a home is conformant when the suite passes with the core unmodified.
svg.text: Kubernetes home
- grant: projected into the Pod by the controller
- ready: the Pod readiness gate
- cgroup: the Pod's own, the agent as PID 1
- endpoint: the Pod IP, a port per fiber
- fabric: one DRA claim per grant
- scope: namespace, service account, claim
- scope lost: namespace or claim gone
- liveness: the API server answers for the Pod
Standalone home
- grant: a file, or inside the first Clone
- ready: the batched Watch stream
- cgroup: a delegated subtree
- endpoint: unix sockets or a declared address
- fabric: a static device list
- scope: none beyond min(lease, fence)
- scope lost: the admin stand-in
- liveness: the issuer's keys keep refreshing
Slurm home
- grant: verified and staged by the launcher
- ready: the allocation's state, plus Watch
- cgroup: the job step's, under its limit
- endpoint: the node address, a port per fiber
- fabric: the allocation's GRES
- scope: job, user, partition, node, CPUs
- scope lost: the job leaves RUNNING
- liveness: scontrol answers for the job

the core, identical beneath every home (pkg/agent, pkg/core, pkg/runtime/host)
agent · ledger · fences and epoch · budget · pressure ladder · audit spool
one host runtime over the backends: proc · runc · gVisor · Hyperlight
conformant iff grant-conform passes with the core unmodified
